topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causes and states its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support cancer evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty surrounding environmental contributions to cancer rather than attributing it solely to inherited predisposition or chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and cellular changes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage, showing how their activity depends on chemical reactions and biological processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require tumour-promoting conditions before cancer develops.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of context-dependent carcinogenicity by explaining developmental susceptibility and recapping the mechanisms that make exposures consequential.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenic exposure and activity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenic exposure and activity is obtained and what limits its interpretation.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment through the lens of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
